INTRODUCTION 
 I, the Chairman of the Depa rtment-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and 
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its 
behalf, present this One Hundred Seventy-eighth Report on the Action Taken by the Department of Science 
and Technology on the recommendations contained in One Hundred Seventieth Report of the Committee on 
Demands for Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Science and Technology. 
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science and Technology 
on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventieth Report of the Department-related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on the Demands for 
Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Science and Te chnology which was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 
26th April, 2007. 
3. There were ten recommendations contained in th e One Hundred Seventieth Report of the Committee. 
Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on  
9th August, 2007. 
4.  In the meeting held on 15th November, 2007 the Committee considered the draft Action Taken Report 
and adopted the same. 
 
 
 
DR. V. MAITREYAN
 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman, 
November 15, 2007 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee 
   on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests. 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

REPORT 
 The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science and Technology 
on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventieth Report of the Department-related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on the Demands for 
Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Science and Te chnology, which was presented to both the Houses of 
Parliament on 26th April, 2007. There were ten recommendations in the One Hundred Seventieth Report of the 
Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendati ons of the Committee were received from the 
Department on 9th August, 2007. 
 The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the Action 
Taken by the Department of Science and Technology are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:----  
NANO SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVE (NSTI) 
1. Recommendation  
 The Committee desires that the Nano Mission proposal made by the Department should be finalised soon. 
The Committee appreciates Indian Institute of Scien ce, Bangalore and Indian Institute of Technology, 
Guwahati for the breakthroughs made on the respective projects assigned to them. It also desires that such 
success stories encourage other institutes to follow suit. 
 The Committee is of the opinion that futuristic technology based on Nano Science holds an important key 
to future development in the world of science. In an increasingly interdependent world where the dividing line 
between academic research and commerc e is increasingly getting blurred, futuristic projects like those based 
on Nano-science can not only raise our living standards but such potential areas can also create wealth for the 
society. The Committee welcomes the idea of separate budget allocation for Nano-mission in budget 2007-08 
as it believes that such a step would help bring the focus back on Nano-research.  
 (Para 9.4.5) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has mounted National Mission on Nano Science and Nano Technology (Nano-Mission). 
It includes components; such as, Basic Research, Human Resource Development and Education, Nano Centres 
of excellence, Public-Private Part nerships in Industrially important sectors and International R&D 
collaboration. The Mission also plans to put in special  efforts towards development and commercialization of 
Nano Technology, not only through public private partnerships, but also by encouraging and enabling the 
private sector to invest in, and leverage, this sunrise technology. Several potential projects have already been 
sanctioned under the Mission. 
Comments 
 The Committee is of the opinion th at the sanctioned projects should  be put in fast track as the 
advantages in such futuristic project s can only be harnessed if they are completed in competitive time 
framework so that benefits from such innovation can be reaped to the maximum. 
S & T PROGRAMMES FOR SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 

2. Recommendation  
 The Committee is of the opinion that agriculture sector continues to be the Achilles heel of our economy. 
With very little growth over the year s, we are entering the danger zone of  increased poverty levels in the rural 
sector. It is in this context th at Science and Society Programme of the Department acquires immense 
importance. The idea of eleven scien ce based organizations to nurture S&T personnel to take up challenges to 
work on rural problems and evolving innovative, S&T based solutions can go a long way in addressing the 
failure of agriculture extension services which is one of the reasons for slow growth of agriculture. 
 The Committee also expresses its satisfaction on the work done by the Department in field-testing and 
adaptation of water filter and desires that such projects should be replicated elsewhere. (Para 10.8) 
Action Taken by the Department 
 The Science and Society Programme of the Depart ment continues to strive to set up S&T-based 
organizations to address rural problems through innova tive S&T-driven solutions. Many more core-groups are 
being considered for support for taking up problems in farm and non-farm sectors. These core-groups will also 
nurture S&T personnel to take up challenges to work on rural problems. In addition, the rural needs are also 
being addressed through Women Technology Parks. 
 The Department has undertaken a demonstration project on the use of satellite data on cooperative 
planning and management in Haryana successfully. There is plan to implement successful experiment to other 
neighbouring States as well. 
 The Department would continue to field-test indigenously-developed technologies for extensive 
utilization of such technologies in different parts of the country. 
Comments 
 The Committee would like the Department to facilitate the use of satellite data for end users so that 
such sophisticated technological fa cilities do not remain esoteric and become end-user friendly for the 
masses. The Committee feels that indi genously developed technologies su itable/useful for local needs of 
farming community should be encouraged in coordination with ICAR as much as possible. 
SYNERGY PROJECTS 
3. Recommendation  
 The Committee notes the reasons for the delay in the commencement of project and would like the 
Department to do its groundwork properly before demanding allocations so that the fund can be optimally 
utilized in future. (Para 11.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted by the Department. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like the department to ensure compliance. 

TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT BOARD (TDB) 
4. Recommendation  
 The Committee is of the opinion that in a competitive economy assistance to technology entrepreneurship 
is of utmost importance. Symbiosis between research initiatives and industry participation is essential for any 
research to become fruitful. The Committee notes the e fforts made in the area of effluent treatment, water 
treatment and power from municipal solid waste. (Para 13.3) 
Action Taken by the Department 
 TDB is a unique organization under Department of Science and Technology, which has played an 
important role in developing technology oriented ventur es in the country, thereby giving boost to Industry as 
well as techno-entrepreneurs. TDB also has been working on development of symbiosis between research 
institutions and industry by not only providing financial support but also provides guidance through experts for 
research to become fruitful by way of commercializat ion of R&D results from various sources. TDB has been 
making efforts by initiating new initiatives to increase th e reach of TDB to build partnerships with academic, 
research institution and industry. 
 TDB has provided seed support funding to Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) Science and 
Technology Entrepreneurship Parks (STEPs) for pr oviding requisite seed support to incubatees for 
development of their projects, which will ultimately be considered. Further, it has investment in few Venture 
Capital Funds to provide support to commercialize innovati ve and technology oriented ventures as well as to 
seed and early stage ventures. 
 TDB by providing financial assistance to the tune of Rs. 800 crore, created-symbiotic partnerships with 
about 180 industrial concerns and 70 national laboratories and academic institutions in the country. The source 
of technology support by TDB is as under: 
(i) In-house R&D centres of industry and commercialized by 
Industry 
49.2% 
(ii) National Labs  21.3% 
(iii) Individuals  10.5% 
(iv) Governments Departments (DAE, TIFAC, etc) 10.0%  
(v) For adaptation of imported technologies by industry 5.2% 
(vi) Academic Institution 3.8% 
 Total : 100.0%                           
 
 TDB is committed to promote development and commercialization of innovative technologies in all 
sectors of industry for overall development of the nation. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. 
5. Recommendation 

 The Committee appreciates .the efforts of the Board for its good financial performance. It is of the 
opinion that the sound financial health is of utmost importance to facilitators like the ‘Technology 
Development Board’ so that financial assistance could be provided to novel ideas and entrepreneurs well on 
time.  
    (Para 13.8) 
Action Taken by the Department 
 The Department has noted the suggestion of the Committee. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.  
SCHOLARSHIPS FOR SCIENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION 
6. Recommendation 
 The Committee supports the idea of widening and streng thening the base of scientific research in the 
country through capacity building in schools, colleges  and universities. The idea  of forming, ‘Science and 
Engineering Research Board’ to fulfil the above objective can be useful and might help in plugging the gaps in 
the supply of quality human resource. (Para 15.3) 
Action Taken by the Department 
 The Department has noted the recommendations of the Committee. As recommended, the Department is 
confident that the establishment of the proposed ‘Science and Engineering Research Board’, which is presently 
at the inter-ministerial consultation level, would widen and strengthen the research base in the country and 
would help reduce the gap between requirements of quality human resources and its supply. 
Comments 
 The Committee desires that the ‘Science and Engi neering Research Board’ provide the necessary 
institutional back up to plug the gap between the requirement and availability of research professionals. 
WATER TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVE 
7. Recommendation  
 The Committee desires that the steps taken by the Department in designing water technologies should 
bear fruits in the near future. Water pollution being a major problem in our country and providing safe drinking 
water a major challenge, the need of the hour is easy availability of low cost domestic water purification 
technology so as to Save people from polluted water and the resultant water borne diseases.  
    (Para 18.4) 
Action Taken by the Department 
 The Department would consciously strive for development of water purification technologies at 
household level so that availability of adequate and safe drinking water is demonstrated widely. The 
Department has already organized a national consultation with scientists and technologists on 28-29 June, 
2007 at Lucknow, which has resulted in identification of specific technologies which could be adopted at field 
level. 

Comments 
 The Committee would like the Department to popularize water purificat ion technologies in 
coordination with all other Depart ments involved in the field so that  they can benefit people in smaller 
towns where drinking water is not purified either  because of lack of  awaren ess or because of costly 
technologies available. 
INNOVATION CLUSTERS 
8. Recommendation 
 The Committee believes that in the fast changing world of today where the growth of technology is 
exponential, both generation of innovative ideas along with their adaptations in the work environment and their 
commercial viability is essential. Helping firms adapt to new production practices is not only important for the 
firms to stay in business but also important to spread a .culture of flexibility and learning so as to remain 
efficient in the long run. The Committee in its interaction with the Department has highlighted the importance 
of not just attracting young people but also empowering them so as to involve them in decision making and 
helping them take up responsibilities so that they can become future leaders. The Committee appreciates the 
idea of innovation clusters to attract young minds. The Committee believes that science research being a 
dynamic field, young scientist should be trained to take fast decision and show functional flexibility.  
 (Para 19.5) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The suggestion of the Committee has been noted by the Department. The Department would integrate the 
suggestion during the implementation of the project. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and woul d like to be apprised in the matter. 
PATENT  FACILITATION  CENTRE (PFC) 
9. Recommendation  
 The Committee attaches great importance to the creati on of Intellectual Property Rights and recommends 
the Department to take necessary steps to ensure that all novel scientific efforts should get translated into 
intellectual property. The Committee would like the Department to set up Technology Intelligence Cell in the 
Department so as to keep track of directions which contemporary science is taking, based on IPR activities. 
    (Para 20.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 Patent Facilitating Centre (PFC) has been providing technical and financial support to all educational 
institutions in the-country for intellectual property rights emanating from innovative research conducted in 
these institutions in India and elsewhere through patents, designs and. copyrights. PFC also helps other 
Government Ministries/Departments in this regard. PFC has been helping DRDO in filing all their patent 
applications and maintaining them. The Department is planning the establishment of an in-house Technology 
Intelligence Cell while engaging also other S & T institutions for data compilation and assessment for tracking 
technology trends and development of technology foresight. 
Comments 

 The Committee notes the reply. 
SECURITY TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVE 
10. Recommendation  
 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department in providing security technology initiative 
which may provide safeguard of national security. This  would also help our security forces in combating 
terrorism.   (Para 21.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has noted the appreciation made by the Committee. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.

REPORT 
 The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Bio-technology on the 
recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventy-second Report of the Department-related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on the Demands for 
Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Bio-technology, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament 
on 26th April, 2007. There were seventeen recommendations in the One Hundred Seventy-second Report of 
the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the 
Department on 17
th August, 2007. 
 The Committee’s recommendations, Action Taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the 
Action Taken by the Department of Bio-technology are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:–  
1. Recommendation  
 The Committee takes note of the gap between the projected demand and the actual allocation made to the 
Department. It is of the view that the Department should make projections that are realistic so that they are not 
reduced at the time of allocation.                      (Para 3.2) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has noted the advice of the Committee. However, the department has prioritized the 
activities to keep the pace of progress within the allocated budget. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and desires that the pace of progress made including outcomes be 
intimated. 
2. Recommendation  
 The Committee desires that the Department should make good use of money allocated for the new 
programmes. It also strongly recommends that the De partment should draw a reasonable time-frame for the 
new programmes and devise a mechanism to monitor their progress so as to prevent themselves from over-
running their schedules.              (Para 3.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The advice has been noted. All the programmes have inbuilt time-frame  and mechanism to monitor the 
progress. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and desires  that the progress made be intimated. 
3. Recommendation  
 The Committee takes serious note of  the underutilization of funds and the consequent time over-runs such 
projects will suffer from. The Committee desires that the problem should be rectified in the coming year as 
promised by the Department.            (Para 3.6) 

Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has taken steps to ensure timely implementation of the projects. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and feels that th e Department give a brief account of the steps 
taken to check underutilization of funds and to ensure timely implementation of the projects. 
4. Recommendation  
 The Committee desires that the reorientation of some of the above programmes, which could not be 
completed, should give them a sharper focus and higher probability of success in the coming years. 
(Para 3.8) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Process and Product Development schemes ha s been reoriented and named as Programme for 
Promotion of Excellence and Innovation which includes schemes on Centres of Excellence and Technology 
Management. 
Comments 
 The Committee would like to be apprised of the e ffect of reorientation in implementation of the 
various programmes. 
5. Recommendation  
 After examining the above proposal  the Committee is of the view that  the above additional requirements 
of the Department, considering the importance of above programmes, should be provided to enable the 
Department to complete its programmes on schedule.        (Para 3.10) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department will make efforts to enhance the provision for these schemes at RE stage. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of th e further developments in this 
regard. 
6. Recommendation  
 The Committee congratulates the Department for meeting its targets set for the Tenth Plan and desires 
that the Department should continue the good work in the next plan.        (Para 4.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department is thankful to the Committee for appreciating the effective and proper management 
during Tenth Plan. The department assures to maintain the pace. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. 

7. Recommendation  
 The Committee appreciates the Department for establishment of International Depository Authority at 
IMTECH, Chandigarh for patent deposits. The Committee has been informed that it is first such facility in 
India, 7th in Asia and 34th in the World. The Committee is of the opinion that in a world of fierce competition 
where piracy of intellectual property is commonplace,  especially in developing countries where awareness 
about wealth generation through intellectual efforts is low, such facilities should be put to maximum possible 
use to save our intellectual property.            (Para 8.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department is thankful to the Committee for ap preciating the establishment of IDA. The department 
is committed to safeguard the intellectual property rights in the area of biosciences. 
Comments 
 The Committee is of the view that safeguarding our intellectual property will remain an important 
area of priority. 
8. Recommendation  
 The Committee would like the Department to expedite its efforts in areas of cancer biology, development 
of drought tolerant crop varieties and research on tuberc ulosis. While the cases of cancer in the country are on 
the rise, we are still far from being a tuberculosis free Nation. A large section of our people belonging to the 
lower strata of the society, who also happen to fo rm a substantial number of the workforce, suffer from 
tuberculosis. The Committee also recommends the Department to work harder to develop drought tolerant crop 
varieties as Indian agriculture is still dependent on th e vagaries of monsoon and crop failures and consequent 
agrarian distress is a recurrent phenomenon.          (Para 8.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has supported a centre of excellence on research on tuberculosis. Drought and salinity 
stress mostly experienced by crops grown in arid and semi - arid regions are some of the most critical factor 
effecting agricultural productivity. Research over the past two decade has provided a better understanding of 
molecular biology of stress responses in plants. Many genes and promoters have been identified and 
biotechnological tools have been applied to transfer some of these  useful genes implicated in stress tolerance. 
In DBT supported programme on development of salinity and drought stress tolerance in rice, over 900 stress 
regulated gene sequences were obtained and sequenced and specific potential genes have been identified. Rice 
and wheat lines transformed with a number of genes to c onfer stress tolerance. Projects are in progress for 
breeding drought resistant sorghum, pearl millet and finger millet through DNA marker assisted selection. 
Comments 
 The Committee while taking note of the work done by the Depart ment to develop stress tolerance 
in rice and wheat also notes that the Department has not reported any wo rk done in the area of cancer 
biology. 
9. Recommendation  

 The Committee welcomes the idea of capacity building in agriculture biotechnology and recommends 
that the Department should carefully choose such agriculture universities so that over a period of time they 
could develop core competency in this area developing centres of excellence to handle most of the agriculture 
biotechnological research in future.             ( P a r a  9 . 3 )  
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has supported four Agriculture Universities for upgradation research facilities & faculty 
member viz. Punjab Agriculture University, Ludhiana, GB Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, 
Pantnagar, University of Agricutural Sciences., Dharwad and Tamil Nadu Agriculture University, Coimbatore. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and th e action taken by the Department. 
10. Recommendation  
 The Committee has been informed that several technologies for vaccines development have been 
transferred to industries. The Committee is hopeful that such vaccines will soon come in the market and will 
be available at affordable prices to the people.           (Para 9.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 Vaccines for rotavirus, diarrhoea, typhoid and ma laria are presently at clinical evaluation stage. 
Comments 
 The Committee is of the view that after clinical trials such vaccin es should be made available to 
people at affordable prices. 
11. Recommendation  
 The Committee is happy to note that the Department has successfully decoded the genome information of 
the rice chromosome number 11. 1t is hopeful that transformation technologies for rice developed for salinity 
and drought tolerance and GM mustard with higher yields is in field testing which showed 45% and 28% yield 
advantages would Soon reach the farmers and help rais e their income lessening so me of the distress Indian 
farmer is presently undergoing.         (Para 10.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 Indian scientists have participated in the International Rice Genome Sequencing Project (IRGSP). The 
Indian scientists have successfully decoded the genome information of the rice chromosome number 11 as part 
of the IRGSP. A network project has been sanctioned last year on development and evaluation of salt and 
drought tolerant transgenic rice. The main objective of the programme is development of rice lines with 
genetically modified stress tolerance serving as pre-bree ding material for transfer of drought and salt tolerance 
trait. 
 The University of Delhi, South Campus (UDSC), Ne w Delhi developed mustard male sterile and restorer 
lines making use of barnase and barstar genes respectively. The male sterility and restorer capacity were 
subsequently transferred to suitable combiners through  recurrent backcrossing for development of DMH-11 
hybrid. The National Research Centre of Rape Seed  Mustard, Bharatpur along with UDSC have been 

conducting the multi-location trials of this hybrid with the permission of regulatory committee to see the yield 
advantages. During the last crop season maximum yield advantage of ( 28%) was recorded at certain locations. 
Further field tests are at more locations worked out. 
Comments 
 The Committee takes note of the reply and woul d like the Department to make available stress 
tolerant rice varieties as soon as possible. 
12. Recommendation  
 The Committee understands the importance of Animal Hu sbandry to the rural sector and is of the view 
that continuous research efforts have to be made to improve the quality of our livestock capital in order to raise 
the income levels of our rural population. The Committee is happy to know that embryos of superior animals 
are being continuously used to pres erve and improve indigenous breeds of cattle and buffalo. The Committee 
desires that the Department should perfect ‘Ovum pick up technology’ making the cost of Embryo Transfer 
affordable.           (Para 14.6) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department is making efforts to enhance the productivity of livestock animals. Emphasis is being 
given to improve the health status of livestock by developing newer animal vaccines & diagnostics. 
Productivity enhancement is being approached throu gh improvement of nutrition and breed improvement 
through various molecular and reproductive techniques. The Department would strengthen and standardize 
various aspects of Ovum Pick up technology for producing a large number of elite animals. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would lik e to be apprised about the progress made. 
13. Recommendation  
 The Committee is of the opinion that the new Gra nd Challenge programmes started by the Department 
which is of interdisciplinary nature should be able to tackle the problem of synergies between diverse areas of 
higher science as scientific research can no long er be divided into water-tight compartments. The 
developments world over in the field of science suggest that the conventional approach of exclusive research in 
clearly defined. scientific areas is no longer relevant. The new target-oriented approach of getting results 
through a combination of inputs from various fields has gained currency. The Committee is of the opinion that 
the above programme should be able to take some of the challenges thrown by higher science.         (Para 15.2) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The programmes to be taken up are: 
 Food and nutrition science and technology 
 Molecular breeding of agricultural crops 
 Molecular breeding of silk worm 
 Microbial prospecting of microbes for industrial, agricultural, environmental, medical and 
therapeutic purposes. 

 Integrated Tuberculosis Research 
 National network for microbicide development 
 Health Science Technology Mission 
- New generation human and animal vaccines and delivery systems 
- Diagnostics for health care 
Stem cell biology and regenerative medicine Bio-design: Implants and Medical Devices 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and the proposed programmes. 
14. Recommendation  
 The Committee expresses its concern over the under-u tilisation of funds allocated for the programme. 
The Committee would like the Department to seriously seek solutions for the problem and draw an effective 
mechanism to monitor progress during the financial year.        (Para 17.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department is engaged in the establishment of biotech parks and incubation centre at a number of 
places in India. These biotech park s and incubation centres provide an excellent template for promotion of 
biotech startup companies. The biotech park at Lucknow  has been established and has attracted several new 
partners in setting up of ventures. The projects at Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka 
are under various stages of establishment and likely to emerge as models of Public Private Partnership. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would lik e to be apprised about the progress made. 
15. Recommendation  
 The Committee supports the idea of  lending a helping hand to existing private industrial units whose 
product development is based on in-house innovative R&D. The Committee believes that financial and 
technical support should be given to individual innovators as good innovations many a times come from the 
unorganised sector. The Committee welcomes the idea of creating opportunities for starting new technology-
based or knowledge-based businesses by science entrepreneurs. Such a step can go long way in spreading the 
culture of knowledge based entrepren e u r s h i p .           ( P a r a  
18.5) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has launched the scheme “Small Business Innovation Research Initiative (SBIRI)” in 
September 2005 to boost public private partnership effort in the country in the areas of biotechnology. The 
SBIRI aims to strengthen private industrial units whose product development is based on in-house innovative 
R&D. The SBIRI scheme operates in two phases viz. SBIRI Phase I support is for highly innovative, early 
stage, pre-proof of concept research, while SBIRI Phase II support is for late development and 
commercialization of innovative research leads. The key objectives of the scheme is to nurture and mentor 

innovative and emerging technologies /entrepreneurs, and to forge appropriate linkages with academia and 
government. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply a nd the initiatives introduced and would like to be apprised about 
the progress made. 
16. Recommendation  
 The Committee believes that the Department should engage in maximum possible cooperation in the field 
of bio-technology with other countries in consonan ce with our national priorities. Opportunities for 
technological collaboration in the fields of agriculture biotechnology, disease resistance and finding new 
vaccines should be sought by the Department to find solutions to our problems in these areas.   (Para 19.5) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 Recommendation have been noted. The Department is already engaged in bilateral cooperation in 
biotechnology which includes the fields of agriculture biotechnology, disease resistance in plants and vaccine 
development. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the progress made in the field of agricultural bio technology. 
17. Recommendation  
 The Committee is of the opinion that there is a lot to learn from the developed countries in the field of 
genetic engineering to address the health needs of ou r country. The Institute can play a pivotal role in 
coordinating scientific and technological exchanges with the west so as to obtain vital inputs for our health 
r e s e a r c h .                ( P a r a  2 0 . 3 )  
Action Taken by the Government 
 International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB) has a focused programme on 
infectious diseases, vaccine and diagnostics development in collaboration with both developed and developing 
countries. 
Comments 
 The Committee is of the view th at more institutes should collaborate in international research 
projects as modern research by its very nature is complex and require varied inputs.

 would be particularly supported for modernization during the year 1995-96.  As regards International Science and

 important activities such as Science and Society Programmes, Assistance to the State Councils on Science and

 National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation (NATMO) will bring out various types of maps which provide
 useful S&T inputs for planning developmental activities. It is trying to develop the new technology of reverse printing
 for NATMO maps on experimental basis. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is making constant endeavours
 to modernise its facilities and to improve the quality of its service. The Committee was told that, under the extension
 programme of DisastEr Warning System (DWS) (Phase-III), 120 DWS receivers are under supply to cover more coastal
 areas. The plan concerning modernisation of seismological observatories has been taken up by IMD. The Committee
 was also given an account of the proposed programmes of IMD for the year 1995-96. National Centre for Medium
 Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) is a multidisciplinary project for which DST has been taking parallel actions to
 develop infrastructural facilities and expert manpower to meet the specific and nationally urgent objectives of the
 project which, inter-alia include setting up of major infrastructural facilties like Supercomputer and Communication
 Network, development, preparation and dissemination of agrometeorological operational advisories, etc. One of the
 proposed programmes for NCMRWF for the year 1995-96 concerns operational issue of medium range weather forecast
 upto three days in 'advance:
 
3. After listening to the presentation made by the Secretary, DST, the Committee examined the budgetary allocation
 of the Department for the year 1995-96'. While considering the Demand~ for Grants of the Department, the Committee
 also got an opportunity to review the work of various projects and programmes which fall within the mandate of the
 Department.
 
4. The Committee had noted in its Twelfth Report the fact that the total Eighth Five Year Plan outlay made for the
 Department by the Planning Commission was kept at     Rs. 640.00 crores. Out of this amount the Department would
 have spent Rs. 563.80 crores till 1994-95. This would mean that the Department would actually be left with an outlay of
 Rs. 76.20 crores for the next two years of the Eighth Plan period. This allocation was hardly sufficient for the
 Department for running its various programmes and activities. The Committee, therefore, wanted to know the outcome
 of the mid-term appraisal of the Eighth Five Year Plan concerning the Department. The Committee was informed that,
 during the mid-term appraisal of the Eighth Five Year Plan in August 1994, DST projected to the Planning Commission
 an outlay of Rs. 1127 crores as against the approved outlay of Rs. 640 crores for the entire Plan period. The Planning
 Commission also recognised that the total requirement of the Department during the years 1995--97 would be to the
 tune of Rs. 521 crores, though the Department had actually projected the demand of Rs. 591 crores for this period. The
 Planning Commission was of the view that the plan outlay for DST for the remaining two years could be finalised at the
 time of formulation of the Annual Plans. As against demand of Rs. 521 crores agreed to by the Planning Commission

4.1 The Committee is of the view that the Planning Commission may consider recommending a sum of Rs. 521
 crores to DST for 1995--97 which it had already agreed and the Department may, if possible, try to get some more
 money during this year while preferring revised estimates.
 
4.2 The Committee expresses its satisfaction over the fact that the Plan allocation for DST has been gradually
 increasing over the years, but in order to increase this allocation in real terms, care has to be taken to neutralise the
 effect of inflationary trends which reduce the actual value of allocation. DST is playing an important role in the
 promotion of science and technology in the country. Services rendered by SO1, NATMO and IMD are valuable. There
 are also many important autonomous institutions which are supported by DST. The Committee, therefore, feels that
 realistic allocation may be made for the Department for the remaining Eighth Plan period.
 
5. In its Twelfth Report the Committee had noted last year that the Department could not utilise its plan funds fully
 and there was excess utilisation on the non-plan side. It was explained to the Committee then that the savings of the plan
 components was mainly due to non-procurement of equipment, and delay in construction activities particularly with
 regard to the building plan of NCMRWF. The Committee was told that this year the revised building plan of NCMRWF
 has been approved by the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC). The two revisions of office and residential complex
 for NCMRWF had resulted in a reduction of the building cost from Rs. 27 crores to Rs. 12.14 crores. The approval of
 the Government was obtained in January, 1995 for the construction of office and residential complex for NCMRWF at
 NOIDA. The contract for the construction of residential complex has been awarded° and it is expected that the
 construction work will start from May, 1995.
 
5.1 On a specific query from the Committee about any surrenders this year from the plan funds, the Committee was
 informed that this year the gap between the allocations made and their utilisation would be very marginal. As against the
 revised estimates of Rs. 213.95 crores of the Department for the year 1994-95 the likely expenditure of the Department
 would be Rs. 213.78 crores. Therefore, the under-utilisation would come to about Rs'. 17 lakhs.
 
5.2 The Committee is glad that in the year 1994.95 the Department could utilise the plan funds allocated to it almost
 fully; this has been possible by permissible reallocation from one plan head to another; accordingly, there are plan
 allocations for specific programmes, e.g., drug design and development that have remained underutilised. The
 Committee hopes that the trend to utilise fully the allocated plan funds would be maintained in the coming years and
 more specifically as earmarked.
 
6. The Committee wanted to know the reasons for the wide gap between the plan an€ non-plan allocation made for
 SOl for the year 1994-95, and the similar trend seen in the budget estimates for the year 1995-96. The Committee also
 wanted to know whether in the past any exercise was done to reduce the non-plan expenditure of SOl. To this, the
 Secretary, DST replied that SOl is a service organisation with assigned charter of duties such as topographic mapping,
 geodetic surveys, etc. The staff for this work is supported under non-plan component. Plan budget is allocated for
 specific new projects and for its modernisation plans. This component, therefore, is small compared to the regular non-
plan activities of SOI. He also informed the Committee that in 1990, SOl fixed staffing norms and field squad strength
 norms for its topographic operations to reduce the non-plan expenditure. Further measures to reduce non-plan
 expenditure were taken such as 10% cut in staff strength and curtailment in office expenses and other austerity
 measures.
 
6.1 The Committee realises the fact/hat SOl is a very old service organ|sation; and, therefore, its non-plan
 expenditure is bound to be higher compared to the plan expenditure. The Committee, however, expresses its concern
 over the continuous rise in the non-plan expenditure of SOI despite the fact that modern tools and technologies of
 survey are available. The Committee, therefore, recommends that DST should prepare a modernisation plan for the
 operations of SOI which should ultimately aim at sharpening the activities of SOI and reducing its non-plan
 expenditure.
 
7. To a specific question about strengthening SO1 to indigenously develop technologies for cadastral surveys and
 observations by fabricating suitable instruments, the Secretary, DST informed that SO1 in February 1992 undertook a
 pilot project in Angul-Nelco sub­division of Orissa for streamlining a procedure for modern cadastral survey. The
 technology of aerial photography is being used for such work for the first time. In order to apply digital mapping
 technology in cadastral survey work, the existing, analog photogrammetric instruments are to be converted into digital
 work stations. This technology of conversion has been developed and is being used in this pilot project. The project is
 still continuing.

 indigenous technologies for cadastrai survey would soon become the strength of SOI. The Committee also hopes that

8. The Committee also wanted to know the steps being taken by DST for bridging the gap between plan and non-plan
 expenditure of IMD. The Committee has, particularly, noticed that there is little increase in the expenditure on the plan
 side in the budget estimates for IMD for the year 1995-96, but on the non-plan side the allocations have been enhanced
 substantially. The Secretary informed the Committee that most of the activities of IMD are service-oriented, and are of a
 continuing nature. These activities are manpower intensive. There is, therefore, little scope for reduction of non-plan
 expenditure. However, over the years, he informed the Committee, that the plan expenditure of IMD is increasing at a
 faster rate compared to non-plan expenditure thus reducing the gap. Taking 1992-93 as the base year, while non-plan

 Committee that development and improvement of seismological system of IMD is being supported to a significant
 extent through allocation from the World Bank/DST budget which was Rs. 3.95 crores during the year 1994-95.
 
8.1 The Committee noted the fact that with regard to SO1, NATMO and IMD the available budgetary figures
 indicates that there was under-utilisation of the allocated plan component, but on the non-plan side the expenditure
 exceeded the approved outlay. The Committee, therefore, feels that while DST should devise methods to curtail the
 growth of non-plan expenditure of these organisations, it should also be seen that the plan component of their budget is
 fully utilised, as this would indicate clearly that these organisations are engaged in promoting scientific activity
 concerning their area of operation.
 
9. In order to strengthen the capabilities for independent drug design and development through a multi-agency, multi-
institutional programme a sum of Rs. 10 crores was allocated to DST last year. The Committee wanted to know about
 the development under this project. The committee had also noticed that in the Budget Estimates for the year 1.995-96
 the allocation for this programme had been reduced to Rs. 6 crores. The Secretary, DST informed the Committee that
 there are two  Committees-one is an Expert  Committee at the operational level and the other is an Apex Executive
 Committee to steer the progress of the programme.   Experts from national laboratories, academic institutions, Planning
 Commission and the related government Departments from the Expert Committee. The Apex Executive Committee is
 headed by the Secretary, DST and representatives from DBT, CSIR and Planning Commission are on it. In both these
 Committees the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals has been given representation.  DST had so far organized
 three ‘Interaction Meets’  at Delhi, Bombay and Hyderabad, in which representatives from pharmaceutical industries,
 financial institutions, national laboratories, etc. participated. These 'Interaction Meets' were organised in order to work
 out the modalities of funding. It has been decided to start collaborative research programmes in the areas of new drug
 discovery, innovative routes for development of generic drugs and intermediates, standardization of traditional
 medicinal formulations and Chiral synthesis of drugs. As regards reduced outlay for this programme in the current year's
 Budget, the Secretary informed that the lower allocation has been recommended by the Planning Commission keeping
 in view the new drug policy under which cess will be utilised for R&D purposes.
 
9.1 The Committee hopes that this programme of DST would help Indian drug industry to be more competitive in the
 world market. But this can come about only if much greater thrust and higher priority is given to this, The Committee
 notes that under the new intellectual property regime, the area of drugs and pharmaceuticals is one which will be
 affected most critically. This area calls for a determined and concerted thrust in terms of indigenous design and
 development. The amount allocated for this area appears to be quite insignificant. The progress on this programme has
 also been slow.
 
10. The Committee wanted to know the progress of the Mission Mode Project on Cyclone Warning and Seismic
 Observation which was formulated by DST during the year 1993-94. The Committee expressed its concern over the
 upgradation and modernisation of the existing seismological network. The Committee was told that Mission Mode
 Project on Cyclone Warning and Seismic Observation was allocated a sum of Rs. 1.85 crores in 1993-94. Assistance of
 the World Bank was secured in 1994-95. The total cost of this project is Rs. 39 crores, with the World Bank assistance
 of Rs. 25 crores (US $7.5 million). Rs. 14 crores would be provided by the Government of India. This is for the
 peninsular shield region. The total duration of the Project is three years and the Project has been formally launched.
 After the meeting of the International Advisory Committee in December, 1994, processing for procurement of
 equipment for upgrading 10 existing seismic observatories of IMD to Global Seismic Network (GSN) standards has
 been pursued. Global tenders for the purchase of the equipment have also been floated. The first batch of trainees will
 be deputed to USA by July 1995. The existing 20 observatories of IMD falling in the peninsular shield region are being
 taken up for up gradation under the World Bank assisted project. Out of the 20 observatories, 8 fall in the coastal region.
 These are at Calcutta, Visakhapatnam and Madras on the east coast, Bhuj, Bombay, Goa, Mangalore and Trivandrum in
 the west coast. In addition, one new observatory has been set up at Bhubaneswar in February 1995. While the
 seismological network for the shield region is being strengthened, for the Himalayan region a comprehensive plan for

11. As regards Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council (TIFAC), the Committee noted that in
 the Budget Estimates for the year 1995~96, the allocations have been reduced to Rs. 5.10 crores from Rs. 7.16 crores
 made last year. The Committee wanted to know the reasons for this. The Secretary informed the Committee that for
 TIFAC the plan allocation for 1994-95 was Rs. 7 crores with a non-plan component of Rs. 16 lakhs. The major
 component of this was meant for Home Grown Technologies (HGT). The Projects on CFC substitutes, CO based
 chemicals and vitamin A were initiated in 1992-93. In 1993-94, High energy rare earth permanent magnet, Flosolver,
 Cobalt recovery, high performance synthetic thickener for substitution of Kerosene in pigment printing and rapid
 diagnostics projects were initiated. Three more projects were initiated during the year 1994-95 which were concerning
 biofertilisers, membrance cell process for Chlor-alkali production and Denox and SO2 oxidization catalysts for pollution
 control. Taking into account the already approved projects under HGT and in view of the Fund for Technology
 Development to be cited, certain HGT projects in the pipeline were focussed on a few select areas. Hence certain
 reductions were made in the Revised Estimates for the year 1994-95 for TIFAC.
 
11.1 The Committee is of the view that TIFAC has a special role to play in providing technology assessment
, forecast
 and information. The Committee hopes that TIFAC would dedicate itself in a more intense manner to its specific
 mandate technology information forecasting and assessment, and have a special thrust relating to patents. The
 Committee noted the fact that a Patent Facility Cell has already been established in TIFAC. The Committee is, however,
 of the view that efforts of various agencies in the area of patenting are not adequate to meet the challenges. There is no
 major effort relating to creation of awareness and understanding relating to patents and the challenges and opportunities
 in this area; nor of training, particularly of patent attorneys. The newly developing area of intellectual property rights in
 the competitive global atmosphere of today calls for far greater concerted efforts than ongoing at present. There is,
 therefore, urgent need for DST to strengthen its efforts in this area. DST should coordinate its efforts with different
 science departments such as DSIR/CSIR, DBT, ICAR, ICMR and Ministries of Industry, Commerce and Law, as also
 technology generating efforts under science agencies of Government, the educational system and private and public
 sector industry. It was never intended for TIFAC to take on individual technology projects. This diverts its attention
 from it principal mandate which is of great current significance.
 
12. The Instrument Development Programme of DST is an important programme. It aims at indigenous development
 and production of instruments. In the budget estimates for the year 1995-96 there is a marginal increase of Rs. 50 lakh
 for this programme over the allocation made in the budget estimates for the year 1994-95. In its Twelfth Report the
 Committee had recommended strengthening the area of Instrument Development.
 
I2.1 The Committee was informed that DST has been promoting and supporting activities related to indigenous
 development of selected instruments for production in the country. This programme is promoted through (i) Instrument
 Development Programme, (ii) TIFAC-Central Scientific Instruments Organisation (CSIO) Joint Board, (iii) Instrument
 Development via SERC Projects & (iv) Instrument Development through DST Institutions. The R&D Instrument
 Advisory Council has identified four critical areas, namely, Analytical, Medical, Test and Measuring, Geo-Scientific
 and Agri-Electronics Instruments which would be supported for instrument development. Under the TIFAC-CSIO Joint
 Board, an updated directory of industries and institutions in the instrumentation area has been brought out. In addition, a
 major study with Strength Weaknesses Opportunities and Threats (SWOT) Analysis has been completed, Further,
 special market surveys and market studies have been conducted in a few selected areas. A number of industry-
institutions interactions have also taken place. These efforts are likely to result in a few major joint projects with
 industry. Through the SERC Programme, a number of projects have been supported involving specific
 instrument/equipment development. Some of the specific examples of successful development of instruments are
 computerised autoclave facility," fabrication of four circle single crystal X-ray diffractomer, infra-red photopolarimetry
 for astrophysical investigations and low energy invert photo emission spectrophotometer. Some of the DST funded
 autonomous institutions like the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Indian Institute of
 Geomagnetism and Indian Institute of Astrophysics have also developed some sophisticated instruments.

 some of the autonomous institutions supported by DST have done good work in this area. The Committee hopes that
 while making allocations for the autonomous institutions supported by ])ST for their modernisation, in a phased manner

 of instrument development. The Committee would like to stress that instruments are the backbone of modern scientific
 and technological developments. An attitude of confidence in being able to design and build ones instrumentation at the
 frontiers of current development is of the greatest importance for advanced research. It is also an area of challenge and
 opportunity to develop ones own intellectual property rights. In this context, the situation obtaining in India,based
 on'imported instruments and related technology is far from satisfactory. A national analysis of the situation and a
 carefully planned strategy for concerted action is called for.
 
13. In view of the liberalised economy and an all pervasive trend towards globalisation, the accreditation of testing
 and calibration activities have assumed importance. The Committee, therefore, wanted to know about the setting up of
 an autonomous body which would deal exclusively with accreditation of testing and calibration laboratories. The
 Secretary, DST informed the Committee that setting up of an autonomous body, the National Accreditation Board for
 Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) is linked with the formation of the National Quality Council. The
 Department has, however, strengthened this programme by developing documents, organising training courses and by
 promoting accreditation activities.
 
13.1 While the Committee appreciates the work done by DST in the area, it notes that the start of this activity goes
 back to a decade and a half ago, and that in the present competitive trade environment, there will be need for
 certification from a variety of angles e.g., quality, environment, etc. Such large scale certification would call for a large
 number of laboratories certified and accredited for this purpose. This is vital for our export drive. DST must, therefore,
 take urgent measures to coordinate its efforts with other Departments, institutions and laboratories to finalise quality
 manuals and the setting up of such a board and a chain of suitably accredited facilities.
 
14.The Department of Science and Technology is the nodal department dealing with the Science and Technology
 Policy of the country and all matters of management, administration, personnel policies, etc. of relevance to science and
 technology. The Committee, therefore, feels that it should be in a position to give an integrated picture of the scientific
 efforts in India.  The department should be in the know about various research programmes being conducted by other
 scientific departments and the R & D components of the Ministries/Departments of the Government which are not
 scientific per se. DST should be able to present a complete picture with regard to the scientific activities of the various
 Government departments, research institutions, universities etc., as a whole. Not only this, it should also be in a position
 to give an idea about the R & D component of private industry and its priorities. With the introduction of the new
 Industrial Policy and consequent liberalisation of the Indian Economy there is a possibility that the type of funding may
 lead to priority to R & D relating to industry and aspects that lead to immediate results. This may possibly give rise to
 reseach in pure or basic science being relegated to the background. This would be unfortunate for the progress of
 science in" the country. The Committee, therefore, strongly feels that DST may have to make concerted efforts to check
 the emergence of any such trend. The Committee is of the view that freedom and autonomy in the functioning of science
 departments is of vital importance. Bureaucratic approaches, in fact, hamper the progress of science. The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that DST should play an active role in ensuring that scientific activities are provided the
 environment in which they can flourish.
15. After considering the' Demands for Grants of the Department of Science and Technology and assessing the progress
 of various important programmes aqd projects administered by it, the Committee recommends that the Demands for
 Grants of Rs. 421.85 crores, as sought by the Department of Science and Technology for the year 1995-96, under
 Demand, No. 72, are in order and may be approved.

 I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, 
Environment & Forests, having been authorised by th e Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present 
this One Hundred Eightieth Report on the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventy-first Report of the Committee on

2.  The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventy-first Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands 
for Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research which was presented to the Rajya 
Sabha on 26
th April, 2007. 
3.  There were fifteen recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventy-first Report of the 
Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendati ons of the Committee were received from the 
Department on 25th July, 2007. 
4.  In the meeting held on 15 th November, 2007, the Committee considered the draft Action Taken Report 
and adopted the same. 
 
 
 
DR. V. MAITREYAN 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman, 
November 15, 2007 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee 
   on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests. 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
REPORT 
 The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred Seventy-first Report of the Department- 
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands 
for Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 26thApril, 2007, There were fifteen recommendations in the One Hundred Seventy-
first Report of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received 
from the Department on 25th July, 2007. 
 The Committee’s recommendations, Action Taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the 
Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: 
- 
1.  Recommendation  
 Budgetary Allocation 
 The Committee recommends that the Department should make efforts to spend funds which have been 
allocated and should take due care to make proposal which could be practically implemented within the time 
frame set up by the Department.            (Para 2.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The views of the Committee have been noted and all Departments will follow the same in letter and spirit 
while formulating the proposals during 2008-09. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the re ply and would like the Department to ensure compliance. 
2.  Recommendation  
 Technology Promotion, Development and Utilisation Programme (TPDU)  
 The Committee is of the opinion that demonstrati on and dissemination of new technologies is as 
important as their development and the Committee expects the Department to leave no stone unturned to 
popularize such technologies, as the ultimate test of their success is market/popular acceptability.          
(Para 3.1.1.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The views of the Committee are well taken. The re search projects assisted under the TDDP and the 
outcome of such projects including the list of new technologies are published in the Annual Report and 
website of the Department. The new technologies developed are transferred to NRDC after specified period for 
commercialization through advertisement and contact with industries. The commercialization of new 
technologies has to be however, within the provision of IPR Act. 

Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like that gradually there is greater self-reliance through 
communication transactions. 
3.  Recommendation  
 Technopreneur Promotion Programme (TePP)  
 The Committee is happy to know that the Department has increased its support to individual innovators 
and has made efforts to expand the reach of the programme so as to cover more innovators. Such 
encouragements are an important first steps in spreading the culture of innovation and out-of-the-box thinking. 
(Para 3.2.2.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 Encouraged by the observations of the Committee, Te PP has further increased outer limits of support to 
independent innovator to Rs. 15 lakh in Phase I and Rs . 45 lakh in Phase II. Further, TePP outreach centres 
funded by DSIR have been increased to 10. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of so me outstanding innovations and 
there impact in civil society in economic and social terms. 
4.  Recommendation  
 Technology Man agement Programme 
 The Committee is of the opinion that technological upgradation of cottage industries and other such 
industries falling in the unorganized sector has to be taken seriously. This will not only improve the cost 
effectiveness of our economy but will also raise income s of the people in these sectors touching lives of 
millions as the majority of workforce belong to the unor ganized sector. But for this to happen the technologies 
have to be small and affordable so that they are business friendly.                 (Para 3.3.6)  
Action Taken by the Government 
 Among the important initiatives taken under the Technology Management Programme, are Analytical, 
Technology status and Development studies. These study reports provide information to Industry, policy 
makers, entrepreneurs, academic and research institutes in the areas of their concern relating to technologies in 
which effective action can be taken to mitigate problems and enhance efficiency. 
 Cognizant that there are many region specific resour ces in different States in the country that have 
spawned industries, which could benefit through further research and analysis in respect of value addition, 
technology upgradation and information dissemination these reports have been taken up to specifically address 
this need. Further, it is well recognized that identification of technology gaps in existing industries in respect 
of important products and processes, including cottage, tiny and small industries in the unorganized sector, is 
an important requirement that needs to be continually ad dressed. There are also a nu mber of areas where there 
is need for indigenous development of technology and for value addition, including rural based technologies, 
in respect of which information collection and analysis is required. 

 Around 20 such studies have been completed in the last five years. Apart from these studies addressing 
specific region based resources, more than 180 technology  status studies of specific products or processes had 
earlier been completed until the late 1990s. Efforts to disseminate the findings of these reports are consciously 
made, to stimulate action, mitigate gaps and facilitate decision-making. 
 These reports cover sector-specific status of techno logy in the country, international trends, gaps in 
technology, research facilities and other such information, in respect of specific identified products and 
processes. 
 Further efforts would be taken to boost this initiative and newer areas and regions calling for attention 
that would benefit such communities at large would be identified and studied in keeping with this 
recommendation, and the findings would be shared across all beneficiaries and stakeholders. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. However, it is of  the view that studies completed until the late 
1990s and also those during the last five years shou ld now be implemented i.e. transfer of feasible 
technologies to small entrepreneurs and cottage industries. 
5.  Recommendation 
 International Technology Transfer Programme  
 The Committee is of the view that the Department should make all efforts to encourage the start-up 
companies and should monitor their growth trajectories so as to improve and encourage the culture of 
entrepreneurship in the country.                     (Para 3.4.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has prepared a proposal for setting up a Fund for Accelerating Start-Ups on Technology 
(FAST). The details of the proposal are being worked out for seeking the approval of the Government. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to know the progress made. 
6.  Recommendation 
 Consultancy Promotion Programme  
 The Committee welcomes the consultancy programme s for small and medium enterprises run by the 
Department. It is hopeful that the Department will do all the needful to ensure the quality of such services so 
that they remain substantial and are not reduced to mere formalities.         (Para 4.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Consultancy Programme would support more programmes in 11
th Plan for setting up Design and 
Engineering services centres and consultancy clinics in important industry clusters to assist small and medium 
enterprises. It is envisaged that such projects even after successful completion would function on self 
sustaining basis and would provide quality services for SMEs. 

Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like the Department to monitor the progress made. 
7.  Recommendation 
 National Research Development Corporation  
 The Committee is of the opinion that commercializing of indigenous technologies and promotion and 
commercialization of inventions is as important as inve ntions themselves if not more. This is only possible 
with dissemination of information to the recipients so that a market for such technologies could be created. 
Development and promotion of rural technology is yet anot her priority area as our farm sector with its own set 
of peculiarities need indigenous technologies suitable to it.         (Para 6.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 As regards commercialization of technologies, 39  new processes were assigned to the NRDC for 
commercialization and it has executed 43 license agreements during the year 2006-07. To promote inventions, 
besides publishing Awishkar and Invention Intelligence on regular basis, NRDC has announced 5 cash awards 
amounting Rs. 5.00 lakh and one WIPO Gold Medal; provided assistance for filing 86 patent applications; 
organized 26 seminars and. training programmes; c onducted 35 patents searches; delivered 43 lectures on 
awareness regarding IPR; provided techno commercial support to 40 promising inventions and financially 
supported one party through ‘Angel Funding’.  
 Further, the Corporation, under its programme “Promotion of Rural and House hold technologies” has 
participated in 5 rural exhibitions to disseminate appropriate rural technologies to the masses; provided support 
to 8 Rural Technology Development and Training (RTDT) centres; initiated the cluster development 
programme - Dairy and Sericulture- to create awareness among the clusters regarding the latest technologies 
available. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. It would like the De partment to make more efforts to disseminate 
such technologies and increase their popularity. It  would also like the Depa rtment to do follow up 
studies on such technologies so as to track their successes and failures. 
8.  Recommendation  
 Council of Scientific and Industrial Research 
 National Laboratories  
 The Committee is of the opinion that the Department should do proper groundwork before making a 
demand for allocation so that it can escape the embarrassing situation of not being able to spend money of its 
projects it initially demanded. The Committee also believes that all possible steps should be taken to prevent 
spillovers from one plan period to another. It should also try to complete its programmes within the time- 
frame it has set for itself.           (Para 9.8.1) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has taken note of the advice of the Hon’ble Committee and all efforts would be made to 
complete activities in a time-bound manner. 

Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and desires better coordination in implementation of budgetary 
allocation. 
9.  Recommendation  
 The Committee appreciates the decision of the Department to break its various programmes being run by 
National Laboratories under following sub-divisions: S upra Institutional Projects, Network Projects, Inter-
Agency projects and Facilities. The Committee is of the opinion that such a division will be helpful in 
developing core-competencies and professional focus.       (Para 9.8.2) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has noted the appreciation. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. 
10.  Recommendation  
 The Committee fully agrees that the present day process of knowledge generation and diffusion is 
characterized by a shift from research based stand alone scientific disciplines to trans-disciplinary and inter - 
institutional networking. The Committee is hopeful that the Department will try novel ways to develop 
synergies in its research efforts to reach latest solutions in the ever evolving research field.   (Para 9.8.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department has following plan: 
 First is to conceptualize, plan and work, in network mode, on R&D of relevance both nationally and 
globally - and to align it with public, private, strategic or social needs as the case may be. There would be a 
strong paradigmatic link between network and PPP modes. 
 Second is to forge viable, defined and scientifically challenging R&D projects in Supra institutional mode 
to make each laboratory a cohesive and close knit unit. This would help align and reinforce the core 
competency of the laboratories. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. It is of the opinion that the plan  formulated by the Department 
should be meticulously implemente d so as to make break throughs in frontier areas of scientific 
research. 
11.  Recommendation  
 National S&T Human Resource Development  
 The Committee recognizes the need of monetary incentiv es to attract young talent to research field, In a 
world where information technology and management streams offer lucrative career options, 
scholarships/fellowships have to keep in tune with the times so as to not only attract new talent but also to hold 

the existing one so that the attrition rate are kept within manageable limits.                  (Para 
10.4) 
Action Taken by the Government  
 The Department notes the concern of the Committee to attract and at the same time retain the talented 
young persons and it will make all efforts in this direction including introducing new scholarships. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would lik e to be apprised on the progress made. 
12.  Recommendation  
 Intellectual Property a nd Technology Management 
 The Committee appreciates the idea of pro-active and planned patenting. The Committee is of the opinion 
that in a globalised environment where competition comes in all possible hues and from different parts of the 
globe, protecting our hard earned fruits cannot be over-emphasized. The Committee desires that the 
Department should do all the needful to protect our intellectual interests.      (Para 11.4) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 During the last three years, CSIR has put special emphasis on the global protection of those inventions 
which are commercially and strategically important for the organization and the country. 
 In order to meet above objective, all the proposals required for patenting are thoroughly scrutinized and 
necessary suggestions are made to laboratories to provid e/generate required data for the above said purposes. 
Similarly, special emphasis has also been laid on the projects arising out of public-private partnership and 
protection of IP generated from such coordinated efforts. 
Comments 
 The Committee would like to be apprised on specific outcomes as a result of these initiatives. 
13.  Recommendation  
 New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative (NMITLI)  
 The Committee notes with satisfaction that during the Tenth Plan NMITLI has created a brand image and 
is viewed today as a benchmark of P ublic Private Partnership (PPP) schemes.  It is also happy about the fact 
that this scheme is benefiting both the Department and its industrial partners. The Committee feels that such 
schemes can serve as a model for future projects as good research can only be successful in the long run only if 
it turns out to be a commercial success as well.        (Para 13.3) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The feeling of the Committee to be a model for future projects is well taken and organization will strive 
to work in this direction. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to  know how the interests of the scientists are 
protected in the scheme. 

14.  Recommendation  
 Setting up of Institute of  Translational Research  
 The Committee is of the opinion that setting up of the new institute will help to focus better on high-end 
clinical research which requires inputs from innumerab le fields, as it involved problems of human existence 
which require a holistic approach the implication of which also involved issues which are not exclusively 
s c i e n t i f i c .                ( P a r a  1 4 . 3 )   
Action Taken by the Government 
 The proposal for setting up such institute will be taken up for consideration by the Competent authority 
during the XI Plan when Committee’s views would be fully incorporated. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply. 
15.  Recommendation  
 After considering the Demands for Grants of the De partment of Scientific and Industrial Research and 
assessing the progress of various important progra mmes and projects administered by it, the Committee 
recommends that the budgetary allocatio n of Rs. 1902 crores under Demand No. 82 (Department of Scientific 
and Industrial Research) as sought by the Department for the year 2007-08 may be approved.     (Para 15) 
Action Taken by the Government 
 The Department is thankful for the Committee for guidance and recommending the outlay of Rs. 1902 
crore to the Government of India. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.
